children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do have a child. I'm asking about my son Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a son named Alex who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep with things like clothes, school supplies, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if your contributions are sufficient for Child Benefit eligibility, I need to know:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month? And is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep. As far as I know, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask one more important question:

**Who does Alex currently live with?** (For example, does he live with his other parent, a relative, or someone else?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16, so age-eligible)
- You live in the UK
- Alex doesn't live with you, but lives with his other parent
- You contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

The key issue here is that you don't live with Alex, so eligibility depends on whether your contributions are sufficient. You need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment to qualify.

**Do you know if the other parent is planning to claim Child Benefit for Alex, or would they be agreeable to you claiming it instead?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and typically the person the child lives with would claim it. If both of you might want to claim, you would need to agree between yourselves who will claim, or HMRC will decide.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: The other parent isn't claiming it and isn't planning to claim it. We've discussed it and they're fine with me claiming it instead.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Now, to complete my assessment, I need to verify one more thing about your contribution amount. You mentioned you contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep.

The current Child Benefit rates are:
- £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child
- £16.95 per week for each additional child

Since you're contributing £30 per week, which is more than the £25.60 Child Benefit amount for an only/eldest child, your contributions meet the threshold.

Let me ask one final question to ensure I have all the information:

**Is there anything else about your situation or Alex's circumstances that might affect eligibility? For example, is Alex in care with the local council, in hospital long-term, or are there any other special circumstances I should know about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. Alex isn't in care or in hospital or anything. He's just living with his other parent and going to school normally.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why you qualify:

✓ **Age requirement met**: Alex is 8 years old, which is under 16
✓ **UK residence**: You live in the UK
✓ **Responsibility for the child**: Although Alex doesn't live with you, you contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep, which exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child
✓ **No conflicting claim**: Alex's other parent is not claiming Child Benefit and has agreed that you can claim it
✓ **No complications**: Alex is not in care or hospital long-term

**What to do next:**
You can now make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. You'll need to apply through HMRC.

**Important things to remember:**
- Only you can claim for Alex - his other parent cannot also claim
- If either you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge
- You must inform HMRC if your circumstances change (for example, if you stop making contributions or if Alex comes to live with you)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
